equity_bridge.item: Non-core property divestment programme, net of tax, costs and timing
equity_bridge.note: ~800 of identified divestments over three years (FY2026 AR p.7: George and Market Street precinct incl. QT Sydney and the George Street cinema, 525 George Street, other non-core hotels and property, two German freeholds). Taken at 80%: capital gains tax and selling costs on assets carried far below valuation (held-for-sale assets are valued at 130.0 against 69.7 book) and proceeds arriving over FY2027-29. The earnings these assets produce (~26 of EBITDA, analyst estimate: QT Sydney net of a retained management fee, the George Street cinema, most of the Property segment's 6.3, other hotels) are removed from the flows from year 1.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-3.0% 3yr, +1.1% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue and EPS and is not usable as a growth anchor: equity is shrinking through FX translation, dividends above earnings and impairments while property is carried at cost well below valuation. The 5-year revenue and EPS figures start in COVID-closed FY2021 and are meaningless. Revenue 3-year CAGR is the only clean series.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner series: statutory FCF less lease principal less SBC (FY2021 13.4, FY2022 70.8, FY2023 -93.4, FY2024 6.9, FY2025 28.9, FY2026 3.5). The 3-year figure is undefined from a negative base. On the statutory series FY2020 onward is overstated by 100-115 a year of lease principal moved to financing by AASB 16. SBC is immaterial, so SBC-adjusted and unadjusted growth do not diverge.

scenario_narratives.base: Hotels deliver the guided ~13 of incremental EBITDA in FY2027 and keep growing as QT Queenstown and LyLo Gold Coast complete and Connect Hospitality adds managed rooms; cinemas hold EBITDA on a smaller 'Fewer, Better' circuit with admissions flat below pre-COVID levels; Thredbo earns around its reduced 143 valuation. The non-core programme realises ~800 gross over three years, the George Street precinct earnings leave, and capex intensity falls from 11% to 6.5% of revenue as the owned-hotel upgrade cycle ends. The Group stays a conglomerate.
scenario_narratives.bull: The asset-light hotel pivot works: Connect Hospitality and the Independent Collection compound fee income at high incremental margins, RevPAR keeps growing in Sydney, Perth and Queenstown, and premium formats plus site exits lift cinema margins on a strong multi-year slate. EBITDA margin reaches 16.2% net of SBC and capex settles at 6% of revenue. The structure review produces a simplification that the market rewards. What this scenario does not capture is a break-up at valuers' property values: that would be worth more than any earnings path here (see inputs.property_memo) and is the main reason the price sits above the bull value.
scenario_narratives.bear: Theatrical windows shorten and a weak slate pushes admissions down while HOYTS takes share; conference and leisure demand softens with consumer confidence; Thredbo strings together poor snow seasons and needs heavier lift and snowmaking capex; unhedged floating debt gets dearer. Revenue grows 2% a year, margins stay near 12%, capex stays at 7% of revenue. Divestments still happen but the structure review ends without a transaction and the property discount persists.

valuation_philosophy.summary: EVT is valued as an owner-operator on the cash its operations leave after rent, tax and the capex needed to keep hotels, cinemas and a ski resort competitive, plus the after-tax proceeds of the property it has said it will sell. That is a deliberately different lens from the one the market is using. At the current price the equity trades near 47x normalised earnings and above property-at-valuation less debt, so the price is underwritten by independent property valuations and the possibility that the structure review releases them, not by earnings. The model's answer is that the operating cash flows do not support the price; the property memo shows how much of the gap asset values can close and how much is left to the review.
key_risks_to_valuation: The divestment bridge is the largest single judgment: 640 (3.92 per share) rests on ~800 gross being achieved, a 20% haircut for tax, costs and timing, and an estimated 26 of EBITDA leaving with the assets. None of the three is disclosed.
A break-up or demerger at or near independent valuations would be worth materially more than any scenario here; the model is structurally blind to it.
Capex normalisation to 6.5% of revenue is a forecast, not a record: capex has averaged ~10% of revenue over FY2023-26, and each 1pp of revenue is worth roughly 1.3 per share in the base case.
Independent valuations can fall as well as rise: Thredbo was halved in FY2026 (292 to 143) and a further tranche is due at 30 June 2027.
Segment detail for the assets being sold was not captured; the split of hotel EBITDA between owned property and fee income is an estimate.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 11.22-16.15
data_sources.financials: EVT.AX_Metrics.csv and kpis (LeasePayments, Depreciation, CashTaxesPaid); FY2026 Annual Report PDF pages 7-11 (normalised result, outlook, property valuations, divestment programme), 50-53 (statements), 68 (diluted shares), 74 (assets held for sale); H1 FY2026 half-year segment table

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average, FY2026 AR note 2.5 (162.522m basic + 0.667m performance rights). Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and there is no buyback.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity: employee share-based payments expense, net of tax, 3,353 ($'000). No net-share-settlement tax line exists.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD build: 10-year ACGB ~4.4% risk-free, 5.5% ERP, beta ~1.0 gives a cost of equity near 10%; floating bank debt at ~6% pre-tax (4.2% post-tax) at ~16% of capital gives ~9.0%. Set at 8.5% because roughly two-thirds of enterprise value is backed by freehold hotel and cinema property that carries a lower asset beta than the operating leases. One WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality (film slate, snow, conferencing) is charged in the flows and the weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The EBITDA margin path is anchored to the company's normalised EBITDA, which is stated before AASB 16, i.e. after the full cash rent (FY2026 lease principal 107.9 + lease interest ~33.4 = ~141). lease_cost_pct_path is therefore zero (the rent is already inside EBITDA), D&A is the normalised figure excluding right-of-use depreciation (78.8), and the 848.7 of lease liabilities is excluded from net debt. Net debt is bank borrowings 541.4 less cash 64.9.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest; equity is wholly attributable.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: reported_fcf is the lease-adjusted figure: the company's own 'operating cash flow after payment of lease liabilities' of 151.1 less capex 144.3 (PP&E 130.9, capitalised finance costs 7.0, intangibles 6.4). The statutory OCF-less-capex figure in the Metrics CSV is 114.7, which is flattered by 107.9 of lease principal sitting in financing. Both are after ~21 of bank interest, so they are levered; the forward build is unlevered.
inputs.fy0_anchors: FY2026 normalised (pre-AASB 16): revenue and other income 1,314.9, EBITDA 174.4 (Hotels 107.2, Thredbo 21.0, Entertainment ANZ 44.0, Germany 19.4, Property 6.3, unallocated -23.6), D&A 78.8, EBIT 95.6, net finance costs 21.4, tax 19.8 (26.7%), NPAT 54.3. EBITDA is 13.6% of the 1,280.6 core revenue base. Capex 144.3 (11.3% of revenue) was inflated by QT Queenstown; FY2024-25 ran 7.6-8.3%.
inputs.property_memo: Independent valuation of the Group's interest in land and buildings is 2,236.6 against a book value of 1,317.0 (FY2026 AR p.11). Thredbo was revalued from 292 to 143 in FY2026. Property at valuation less net debt is 1,760, or 10.79 per share, before any value for the leased cinema circuit, hotel management fees and corporate costs. A rough sum of parts at valuers' numbers (leased cinemas ~300, management platform ~180, corporate costs ~-190; analyst estimates, not disclosed) lands near 12.6 per share before tax on realisation. The owner-FCF value sits below this because valuers capitalise pre-tax hotel earnings at 6-7% while the model discounts post-tax, post-capex flows at 8.5%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF on the continuing operations, with the ~800 non-core property divestment programme valued separately in the equity bridge and its earnings removed from the flows (matching-asset rule). Routed as a non-US cyclical operating company with material leases. A full NAV or AFFO route was rejected because EVT is an owner-operator, not a rent collector: its hotel and cinema earnings are operating profits that need capex, and the independent valuations are going-concern values of those same earnings. A deal-completes/deal-breaks frame was rejected because the Rothschild-advised Group structure review has produced no transaction, price or timetable; it is carried in the bull narrative and the weights instead. SBC: 3.4 (0.26% of revenue) is already inside normalised EBITDA as employee expense, so the EBITDA margin path is stated 0.3pp above the normalised margin and the engine's explicit SBC line takes it back out, charging it once. Interest income (1.5) is not stripped because the Group is in net debt. No buyback: the flat share count is a convention funded by nothing, but the rights pool is 0.4% of the count. Price is the Friday ASX regular close. FY2026 and FY2025 annual text extractions are digit-corrupted; every FY2026 figure here was read off the PDF pages (7-11, 50-53, 68, 74).

base.rationale: Year 1: FY2027 EBITDA of ~190 before divestments (174.4 + ~13 guided hotel initiatives + ~6 Entertainment on a strong slate - ~4 Thredbo on a poor winter opening), less ~26 for the non-core assets valued in the bridge, is ~164-166 on revenue of ~1,319 (about +6% from a full year of Connect Hospitality and QT Auckland, less ~3pp of divested revenue). Margin then builds 1.8pp over five years as QT Queenstown and LyLo Gold Coast complete, fee income grows and marginal cinema sites exit. Capex falls from 9% to 6.5% of revenue as the owned-hotel upgrade programme finishes; it stays above D&A because Thredbo lifts and snowmaking and cinema refits are recurring. Cash tax at 29% (Australia 30%, NZ 28%, Germany ~30%; normalised effective rate 26.7%) on unlevered EBIT.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% default: every division is discretionary and two of them depend on things management cannot influence (film supply, snowfall), and guidance has been trimmed repeatedly on redevelopment delays; there is no solvency risk given 2.2bn of property against 0.5bn of debt, which stops it going higher. Base 50%: FY2027 guidance and the announced divestment programme. Bull 30%, below the 35% default: it needs the hotel fee platform, the cinema margin story and capex discipline to all land together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
